paras: The stoning of Jacob Clarkson was a street attack on 29 June 1903, at the corner of Fifth and Franklin streets, evidently in Wilmington, Delaware, in which three youths shouted "Lynch the nigger" at Clarkson, a Black man, and threw stones at him. The three were convicted of disorderly conduct in City Court the next day and fined $5 and costs each. The case survives only as a short item in the Wilmington Evening Journal's court column.

According to Clarkson's testimony, he was passing the corner of Fifth and Franklin streets when the three defendants "yelled after him, 'Lynch the nigger,' and winded up by hurling stones at him." The court report names the three as John O'Neill, Arthur Nichols and Howard Barney and calls them "three youths," without giving their race or ages. It mentions no injury to Clarkson, no reason for the attack and no accusation against him.

O'Neill, Nichols and Barney were arraigned in City Court on 30 June on a charge of disorderly conduct, with Clarkson testifying against them. Each was fined $5 and costs, the same penalty the court gave that morning to two other men in unrelated disorderly-conduct cases. No further proceedings appear in the coverage.

The Evening Journal printed the case on its front page on 30 June as the last paragraph of a City Court column headed "Linden Fined for Assaulting Mustard," after reports of an assault, a tobacco theft and a pistol case. The paper quoted the slur as Clarkson reported it and added no comment, treating the matter as one more minor police-court case. No other white paper and no Black newspaper is known to have reported the incident.

reader.title: Stoning of Jacob Clarkson
bases: Three youths shouted a lynching cry at a Black man passing a street corner and threw stones at him; the court treated it as disorderly conduct, and no killing, seizure or custody is reported (A2).

Clarkson was not killed; three youths shouted "Lynch the nigger" and threw stones at him, an illegal act by a group of three, but no attempt to seize or kill him and no accusation against him is reported (A2).
The incident is known only from one City Court report in the Wilmington Evening Journal, based on Clarkson's testimony (A2).
